summary: Four rules about erech: whose money counts, whose age counts, who counts as a man or a woman, and which time counts. First: what a poor person can afford depends on the one who promised.

chunks.en: What a person can afford depends on the one who made the vow.
chunks.explain: A poor person who cannot pay the full erech pays what he can.
chunks.st: Affordability, which is written in the Torah: “According to the means of him who vowed shall the priest valuate him” (Leviticus 27:8), is determined in accordance with the means of the one taking the vow,

words.en: depends on the one who vows

chunks.en: The age depends on the person whose erech was promised.
chunks.st: and the sum fixed by the Torah based on the years of age is in accordance with the age of the subject of the vow.

summary: With a metzora's korban, what counts is the metzora who needs it. Rebbi says erech works the same way when a poor person promises what a rich person promised.

chunks.en: But with korbanos it is not like that.
chunks.st: But with regard to offerings that is not so,

chunks.en: For if someone said,
chunks.st: as one who took a vow and said:

chunks.en: "I will bring the korban of this metzora,"
chunks.explain: A metzora brings korbanos when he becomes tahor from tzaraas.
chunks.st: It is incumbent upon me to provide the offering of this leper,
chunks.stMore: to a leper who requires it for his purification;

chunks.en: if the metzora was poor,
chunks.st: if the one undergoing purification was a destitute leper,

chunks.en: he brings a poor person's korban.
chunks.st: the one who took the vow brings the offering of a destitute leper,
chunks.stMore: which is one male sheep, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, and two doves or two pigeons (see Leviticus 14:21–22).

chunks.en: If the metzora was rich, he brings a rich person's korban.
chunks.st: If the one undergoing purification was a wealthy leper, the one who took the vow brings the offering of a wealthy leper,
chunks.stMore: which is two male sheep, a ewe, and three-tenths of a ephah of fine flour (see Leviticus 14:10).

summary: A metzora's korban depends only on what he has now, even if he will soon get lots of money.

chunks.en: But with korbanos it is not like that.
chunks.explain: His korban depends on how rich he is when he brings it.
chunks.st: But with regard to the offerings of a leper that is not so,
chunks.stMore: as the offerings that one brings are determined by his status at the time he brings them.

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ אָבִיו מֵת וְהִנִּיחַ לוֹ רִבּוֹא,
chunks.en: Even if his father died and left him ten thousand coins,
chunks.st: Even if it is common knowledge that his father died and left him an inheritance of ten thousand dinars,

chunks.en: or his ship is at sea and is bringing him ten thousands,
chunks.st: or that his ship is at sea and merchandise valued at ten thousand dinars is coming into his possession,

chunks.en: the Beis Hamikdash has no share in that money.
chunks.st: the Temple treasury has no share in it.
chunks.stMore: His payment is determined solely by his present situation.
